Daily Briefings · Friday, November 6, 2026

Space & Defense Daily — Friday, Nov 6, 2026

Space Force may need ~$1B in translator satellites because SpaceX’s SDN Backbone lasers can’t talk to SDA and SSC missile-warning birds; NATO opened a counter-drone marketplace and begins German-led drills in Lithuania as France extends Black Sea maritime patrols; Europe nears a Nov. 30 pick between HYDIS and HYDEF hypersonic interceptors.

← NewerMon, Nov 9, 2026All briefingsOlder →Thu, Nov 5, 2026
NATOEuropean UnionUnited StatesEuropean spaceGlobal space & defense

Top stories: Breaking Defense reports the Space Force’s SpaceX-built Space Data Network Backbone uses proprietary optical terminals incompatible with SDA and SSC missile warning/tracking satellites, driving plans for a dozen Space Exchange Point “translator” birds that could cost about $1 billion—critical for Golden Dome connectivity. NATO launched a Counter-UAS marketplace with 16 selected solutions and €3.1 million in testing funds, while more than 6,000 Allied troops start German-led exercises in Lithuania and France extends its Atlantique 2 Black Sea patrol after deadly merchant-ship strikes. And the European Commission is expected to choose by Nov. 30 between the HYDIS (MBDA-led Aquila) and HYDEF consortia for the next phase of Europe’s endo-atmospheric hypersonic interceptor.

NATO

  • NATO launched a Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems marketplace on Nov. 5 under the Drone Edge initiative, letting Allies buy from a catalogue without further tenders; NCIA selected 16 solutions from Alta Ares, Axon Enterprise, Northrop Grumman, OSL UK and Quantum Systems, and allocated €3.1 million for further testing alongside a wider Allied pledge of more than $40 billion in counter-drone spending over five years. (NATO)
  • More than 6,000 NATO troops begin two German-led exercises in Lithuania—Freedom Shield 26-II and Grand Eagle 26—from Nov. 6 to Dec. 3, drawing Germany’s 45th Armored Brigade Lietuva and 37th Mechanized Infantry Brigade plus Multinational Combat Brigade contingents from the Netherlands, Norway, Czechia, Croatia, Belgium and Luxembourg. (Anadolu Agency)
  • France is extending its Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft’s stay at Romania’s Mihail Kogalniceanu base by several weeks after deadly sea-drone strikes on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria; the plane detected drones that sank Contship Jet on Oct. 28 but cannot intercept them, and NATO reiterated its “ironclad” Black Sea commitment. (gCaptain / Reuters)
  • NATO Allied Command Transformation released footage from one of its largest operational experimentation events in Latvia, where more than 30 countries and 100 industry partners used AI agents and nearly 400 drones in the Federated Unified Sensing and Effects (FUSE) trial to link sensors, networks and counter-drone effects. (NATO)

European Union

  • The European Commission is expected by Nov. 30 to downselect either HYDEF (Spanish Missile Systems / Diehl Defence) or HYDIS (MBDA Aquila, with Thales, Leonardo, Saab and others) for Phase 2 of the Endo-Atmospheric Interceptor program, with €100 million in EDF funding, a system demonstrator targeted for 2030 and in-service around 2035; HYDIS pitches a four-stage Mach-17-capable interceptor networked to European space early-warning concepts. (Breaking Defense)
  • At Euronaval, MBDA said its HYDIS team aims to fly a full-systems “fat” hypersonic interceptor demonstrator by end-2029, expand to 17 countries with €133 million in national add-on funding, and undercut SM-3 unit cost while covering both ballistic and hypersonic threats—Germany is dropping out as a Phase 2 partner country. (Defense News)
  • Internal German defence ministry notes obtained by Politico warn that moving too fast to cut dependence on U.S. arms—37% of Germany’s major imports in 2021–25—could strain ties with Washington even as the Commission pushes EU countries toward 50% European procurement by 2030; Berlin still eyes joint work on Patriot ammo, SM-2/6, Tomahawk and AMRAAM. (Politico Europe)
  • Leonardo’s board approved 9M2026 results with an order backlog of €60.4 billion (+28%), new orders of €23.3 billion and adjusted net result of €812 million (+74%), citing GCAP, Rheinmetall and Baykar JVs, the Airbus–Thales space alliance and Michelangelo Dome as strategic priorities after the Iveco Defence acquisition. (Leonardo)

United States

  • Sources tell Breaking Defense that SpaceX’s SDN Backbone “Plaser” optical terminals cannot directly talk to SDA Tracking Layer or SSC MEO missile-warning birds—and those two also differ from each other—so the Space Force is eyeing 12–13 Space Exchange Point translator satellites at roughly $1 billion to stitch Golden Dome’s sensor-to-shooter network together; SSC has already awarded five SEP prototype host contracts. (Breaking Defense)
  • Space Systems Command awarded Viasat a $450 million IDIQ (initial $115 million task order) to build and scale the SDN Backbone mission operations center that will integrate multi-vendor constellations for the Space-Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio supporting Golden Dome. (GovCon Wire)
  • With Democrats set to control the 120th Congress, Space Foundation analysis flags risk to the proposed $1.5 trillion Pentagon topline, a Space Force request above $71 billion and $18 billion more for Golden Dome; experts say another continuing resolution is likely and the branded Golden Dome program is an easy one-time-money target even if core Space Force funding holds. (Space Foundation)
  • NASA selected Astranis ($264.3M), Global Enterprise Solutions ($340.4M) and Viasat ($460.9M) under NextSTEP-3 to develop Ka-band commercial relay concepts that keep legacy missions online as the agency retires its Tracking and Data Relay Satellite fleet. (NASA)
  • SpaceX is targeting Friday, Nov. 6 at 4:46 p.m. PT (backup Nov. 7 at 4:32 p.m. PT) for the classified USSF-432 Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg SLC-4E, with droneship recovery in the Pacific on a booster’s eighth flight. (SpaceX)
  • ULA CEO Mark Peller said Vulcan’s Nov. 13 Amazon Leo return-to-flight from Cape Canaveral SLC-41 incorporates GEM 63XL nozzle mitigations and BE-4 oxidizer-valve retrofits; Space Force Vulcan missions stay on hold pending that flight’s performance as the SRB investigation continues. (Aviation Week)

European space

  • ESA and EUMETSAT released first rapid-scan imagery from Meteosat Third Generation Imager-2 (MTG-I2), showing Europe and northern Africa at 2.5-minute intervals over 45 hours from Nov. 3—fog, Mediterranean convection, opposing Atlantic cloud layers and a Portuguese wildfire plume—from geostationary orbit about 36,000 km up. (ESA)
  • Airbus published a Nov. 6 overview of Spanish Air and Space Force modernization, highlighting Eurofighter Halcón growth to 115 jets by 2035, C295 maritime patrol, SIRTAP and Eurodrone UAS, PAZ radar satellites (two more due 2031) and SpainSat-NG secure communications built with Hisdesat. (Airbus)

Global space & defense

  • China launched Yaogan-51 satellites 07–09 on a Long March-2C from Xichang late Nov. 5 (Long March’s 675th flight); state media calls them remote-sensing/scientific assets, while Western analysts assess the Yaogan-51 triplets as passive ELINT ship-trackers now nine strong for Indo-Pacific coverage. (CGTN)
  • TechTimes’ open-source read of the same launch argues three Yaogan-51 triplets now enable near-persistent passive TDOA surveillance of Taiwan, South China Sea and Korean approaches, days after a DIA report put China’s ISR fleet above 510 satellites. (TechTimes)
  • CesiumAstro announced a $730 million Series D on Nov. 5 valuing the Texas antenna specialist above $4.5 billion as it pivots toward operating its own connectivity constellation. (SpaceNews)
  • Blue Origin announced Nov. 5 it will develop a new third stage (GS3) for New Glenn high-energy missions plus a new booster engine. (SpaceNews)
  • AST SpaceMobile said Nov. 6 it will develop its own Blacklift rocket using Firefly Aerospace engines after launch-vehicle delays slowed its direct-to-device constellation. (SpaceNews)
